matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: Focal Loss reshapes the standard cross-entropy by down-weighting the contribution of well-classified examples, allowing effective training under extreme foreground-background class imbalance.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: The focal loss down-weights the loss assigned to well-classified examples to address class imbalance.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: Hard negative mining and online hard example mining are insufficient to address the dense one-stage class imbalance that Focal Loss handles by reweighting.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: The focal loss outperforms the best variants of online hard example mining by over 3 points AP.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: The accuracy gap between one-stage and two-stage detectors is closed by addressing class imbalance with a loss reweighting rather than by adding architectural complexity.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: The extreme foreground-background class imbalance during training is the central cause for one-stage detectors trailing two-stage detectors in accuracy.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: RetinaNet built on a ResNet-101-FPN backbone reaches roughly 39 AP on COCO test-dev, matching or exceeding two-stage detectors at comparable inference speed.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: RetinaNet with ResNet-101-FPN achieves a COCO test-dev AP of 39.1 while running at 5 fps.

unmatched_a.a_claim_text_normalized: An alpha-balanced cross-entropy alone is not sufficient to overcome extreme foreground-background imbalance in dense detection, motivating the modulating term that focal loss adds.

unmatched_b.b_claim_text_normalized: The focal loss focuses training on a sparse set of hard examples and prevents easy negatives from overwhelming the detector.

unmatched_b.b_claim_text_normalized: RetinaNet with focal loss matches the speed of previous one-stage detectors while surpassing the accuracy of all existing state-of-the-art two-stage detectors.
